event.felix_heart2.0.text: Mornin'. Take the rod. Both hands. Hold the line, [player].
event.felix_heart2.0.why: hands over his own rod: trust before words

event.felix_heart2.1.text: Feel that? Don't reel yet. Let it run. It's deciding about you.
event.felix_heart2.1.why: patience lesson with a joke on the end

event.felix_heart2.2.text: Keep it. You earned it. I'm on this rock at six most days. ...Just saying where the rock is.

event.felix_heart5.0.text: Mornin'. Every fisher has a lucky charm. Mine's sat through forty years of dawns.
event.felix_heart5.0.why: fisher not sailor; forty years alone, unspoken

event.felix_heart5.1.text: It was mine. It's yours now. I don't need luck on the mornings you're here.
event.felix_heart5.1.why: gives away the charm because the player replaced it

event.felix_heart5.2.text: Fair winds. ...Someday I'll show you the boat. She leaks, but politely.

event.past_the_point.0.text: Mornin', both. Boat's ready. She leaks, but politely. The bailing's the elegant part.

event.past_the_point.4.text: Told you, partner. Dawn's better with two. Better with a list, too. ...Forty-one to go. I'll bring a second bailing tin.
event.past_the_point.4.why: warm close that points at the rest of the list

event.story_whistler_felix.intro.text: Oh. You heard that. ...Don't tell the fish.
event.story_whistler_felix.intro.why: drops the stage directions from speech; caught mid-tune

dlg.story.whistler.felix.0.text: I only whistle when I'm happy. Lately that's most evenings. The fish have noticed.
dlg.story.whistler.felix.0.why: subtext: happy since the player came

dlg.story.whistler.felix.r0.text: Hello. Yes. Hello back. Very sensible, given the circumstances.

dlg.story.whistler.felix.r1.text: You got the wrong note exactly right. I'm moved. Also mortified. Mostly mortified.

dlg.story.whistler.felix.r2.text: You listened. The whole tune. Nobody's done that but the pond. ...I may whistle again. Quietly.

event.story_whistler_felix.after.text: Same hour tomorrow, I'll be whistling by the pond. You can pretend you were passing.
event.story_whistler_felix.after.why: a dusk appointment as a thread

event.story_pumpkin_felix.intro.text: Ah. Caught. I only borrowed it. I wanted it beside my biggest carp. For scale.

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.0.text: Behind the store, Felix stands beside a very large pumpkin, wearing a very guilty face.
dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.0.why: narration: present tense, only what is seen

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.2.text: ...It might be. The goats were very understanding about it.

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.c2.text: Offer to carry the heavy end.

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.r1.text: An apology. Yes. I'm sorry, Tilda. Truly. ...And sorry to you, pumpkin.

event.story_pumpkin_felix.after.text: Back it goes, with the photograph. Tilda can frame it. The carp still hasn't forgiven anyone.
event.story_pumpkin_felix.after.why: first person now; carp grudge last

event.festival_winter_lanterns.2.text: My wish is this big. Last winter it was this big. Wishes grow, like fish.
event.festival_winter_lanterns.2.why: his running bit, kept private as Hazel asked

event.felix_heart8.intro.text: Mornin'. The pond, and a line that's tugging. I've had a feeling all week. Hold the net. Don't breathe.

dlg.felix.big.1.text: It's this big. No, this big. ...Partner, what do we do?
dlg.felix.big.1.why: the fish grows mid-sentence; asks the player

dlg.felix.big.r0.text: The net! Hold steady. ...There she is! A beauty. I'll never doubt your wrist again.

dlg.felix.big.r1.text: Let it go? ...Right. A good fish deserves a long life. We keep the story. It's bigger anyway.

dlg.felix.big.r2.text: Honestly. Fine. Eleven inches. ...It was this big a moment ago. I blame the light.

event.felix_heart8.after.text: {if choice:big.net}Netted. It was this big. By Friday it'll be this big, and Tilda will groan.{else}{if choice:big.release}Gone home. It waved, I'm sure. Same dawn next year, we said. We've an understanding.{else}Eleven inches. Honest inches. I'm devastated. And proud. Mostly devastated.{/if}{/if}
event.felix_heart8.after.why: each branch leaves a day or a person

event.felix_birthday.intro.text: It's my birthday. Tilda says no fishing today. She brought a pie. I brought a story. It's about a fish.

dlg.felix.birthday.r0.text: Thank you. I'll tell the fish. They won't care, but I'll feel taller.

dlg.felix.birthday.r1.text: Sit, then. It was dawn, it was this big, and it was smirking at me.
dlg.felix.birthday.r1.why: starts the tale instead of thanking

event.felix_birthday.after.text: {if choice:bday.felix.wish}The fish know it's my birthday. They're pretending they don't. Rude, but traditional.{else}{if choice:bday.felix.story}The story's longer now. I added a hand. And you, at the end, holding the net.{else}Dawn, the pond, and two lines. Best present I've had in forty years.{/if}{/if}

event.felix_courtship.intro.text: Well. Right. I've held a line through a gale. This is harder. Would you court me? Slowly, like the tide.

event.felix_courtship2.intro.text: Well. Right. Second cast. You asked for time, and I gave it. Would you court me? Still slowly.
event.felix_courtship2.intro.why: the second ask acknowledges the first

dlg.felix.courtship.r0.text: Yes! Oh. Best catch of my life, and I wasn't even holding a rod. Dawn tomorrow. The good rock.

dlg.felix.courtship.r1.text: Friends. That's a fine thing. The best dawn partners are friends. I'm glad. I'll be a bit quiet today.
dlg.felix.courtship.r1.why: graceful, with the hurt left in

dlg.felix.courtship.r2.text: A little time. Good. Fish take time. So does the rest of it.

event.felix_courtship.after.text: {if flag:choice.courtship.felix.yes}Dawn, the pond, two lines. I'll bring the thermos. You bring yourself. That's plenty.{else}{if flag:choice.courtship.felix.friends}Friends, then. Still my dawn partner. The rock has room for two.{else}Time, then. The pond's patient. So am I. Mostly.{/if}{/if}
event.felix_courtship.after.why: keeps the dawn standing in every branch

event.felix_courtship2.after.text: {if flag:choice.courtship.felix.yes}Dawn, the pond, two lines. Worth the wait. I'll bring the thermos.{else}{if flag:choice.courtship.felix.friends}Friends, then. Still my dawn partner. The rock has room for two.{else}More time, then. I've waited forty years for a partner. I can wait a season.{/if}{/if}

event.felix_partners.intro.text: Mornin'. I caught something for you. Not a fish. A shell. A very good one. Hold it to your ear.
event.felix_partners.intro.why: his greeting; no sitting the engine can't show for the player

dlg.felix.partners.0.text: Tide's out. Morning's ours. What'll it be?
dlg.felix.partners.0.why: scene plays in the morning, not evening

dlg.felix.partners.r1.text: Two lines and the good rock. You hold the rod. I'll hold the thermos. Finest morning there is.

dlg.felix.partners.r2.text: The sun comes up. We don't say much. The fish don't mind. Neither do I.

event.felix_partners.after.text: {if choice:courtship.felix.shell}The shell sits on my shelf, by the best hook. It still says your name. Or 'hello'.{else}{if choice:courtship.felix.fish}Two lines, one very small fish. Best catch in years. We threw it back.{else}The sunrise was quiet. So were we. Longest conversation I've ever had.{/if}{/if}

event.overheard_tilda_felix_1.l2.text: It's a bigger carp. It grew. In the stall, overnight, out of pride.

event.overheard_tilda_felix_1.l4.text: Fine. Six. The story's two more. It's a very good story.

event.overheard_tilda_felix_2.l1.text: Tilda. Remember the winter the pond froze, and I fell in?

event.overheard_tilda_felix_2.l3.text: Same winter. A long one. You brought me soup. ...Both times.

event.overheard_tilda_felix_3.l1.text: Tilda. I chalked the year's first fish on your slate. Capital letters.

event.overheard_tilda_felix_3.l3.text: It was this big. Bigger, since I chalked it. Don't tell the pond.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_3.l3.why: the fish grows on the slate

event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l1.text: Tilda. I brought a pie, for once. A fish pie. Don't judge it.

event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l3.text: A fair sentence. Pass the fork. ...And the salt.

event.overheard_felix_elara_1.l1.text: Elara. A fish doesn't want a cozy net. It wants to be free.

event.overheard_felix_elara_1.l3.text: ...It does look warm. Give it here. For science.

event.overheard_felix_elara_2.l1.text: It was this big. Bigger. Bigger every time I tell it.

event.overheard_felix_elara_2.l3.text: A scarf and a fish, friends. I like it. Tell no one.

event.overheard_felix_elara_3.l1.text: Dawn's quiet, yes. Until you count stitches out loud.

adds.text: Now! Up, easy. ...A tuna. First try. Took me eleven summers.
adds.why: the bite, and his pride in the player

adds.text: And fifteen bait, hand-dug. Don't tell the stall I gave it away.
adds.why: covers the bait gift, in voice

adds.text: Bring both. The tin floats. The life jacket can sit up front and look brave.
adds.why: Felix welcomes Elara's knitting without mocking it

threads.felix_heart2: Will the player turn up at his rock at six?
threads.felix_heart5: The boat that leaks politely: when will he show it?
threads.past_the_point: Forty-one places left on Elara's list, and Felix means to row them.
threads.story_whistler_felix: He'll whistle by the pond at dusk tomorrow: will the player pass by?
threads.story_pumpkin_felix: Tilda's framed photograph, and a carp that holds a grudge.
threads.felix_heart8: How big will the fish be by Friday, or next year?
threads.felix_birthday: The fish story now has the player in it.
threads.felix_courtship: Dawn at the pond, with a second line.
threads.felix_courtship2: Dawn at the pond, after the long wait.
threads.felix_partners: The shell on his shelf, and the mornings that follow.
threads.overheard_tilda_felix_1: What story is worth two coins?
threads.overheard_tilda_felix_2: The winter he fell in twice, and Tilda's soup.
threads.overheard_tilda_felix_3: The year's first fish, chalked on Tilda's slate.
threads.overheard_tilda_felix_4: Who salts the pie: the feud goes on.

notes: dlg.felix.courtship.* keys are shared by felix_courtship and felix_courtship2; rewritten once.
dlg.felix.partners.0 said 'Evening's ours' in a scene gated 06:00-14:00; changed to Morning.
event.story_whistler_felix.intro had stage directions inside spoken text; removed. The story_pumpkin after line was third-person in Felix's mouth; now first person.
